newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss franc ends lower as dlr rises over 1.50 Sfrs.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc ends lower as dlr rises over 1.50 Sfrs.

text.p: 1530 GMT - The Swiss franc ended lower with the dollar rising to roughly 3-1/2 year highs, breaking above the key 1.50 franc level for the first time since December 1993.

Swiss traders said the franc's drop against the mark was likely due mainly to stop-loss orders. There were rumours in foreign markets that the Swiss National Bank had intervened, but one currency trader here dismissed this as "complete rubbish." A second Swiss trader said that the SNB was not active in the domestic money market in the afternoon, either.

The Swiss National also has directly intervened only rarely in open currency markets. According to a study published in the SNB's quarterly bulletin of second quarter 1996, the SNB intervened independent of other central banks in the period from 1986 to 1994 only three times.
The SNB also said in the study that if it does conduct such intervention it has usually made clear to banks that it was operating in the open market, its study said.
One trader said that mark/Swiss gained on stop-loss buying at mark levels above 81.20 centimes. Thursday's European low was 80.90.
One trader said there was also active dollar buying above 1.49 Swiss francs.
* The dollar ended at 1.4975/4980 Swiss francs compared with 1.4850/60 at the open and 1.4860/4870 at Tuesday's close.
*The mark ended at 81.81/81.84 centimes versus 81.33/42 Swiss centimes at the open, and 81.24/26 centimes Tuesday. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
